exposure: Laparoscopic wedge resection of cornual ectopic pregnancy
laparoscopic wedge resection of cornual ectopic pregnancy
cohort: 20 women with uterine rupture observed in the delivery room of a Taiwanese tertiary obstetric center over a 15-year period
finding: The study found an overall uterine rupture rate of 3.8 per 10,000 deliveries, with non-CS ruptures (59%) being more common than CS ruptures (32%), and all non-CS ruptures occurring in women with a history of laparoscopic procedures to the uterus.
mod_finding: Severe bleeding requiring transfusions was more frequent in women who experienced non-CS compared with CS ruptures.
